prerequisites: Ability to read and comprehend texts written in English

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and implement the parallel programming paradigm based on distributed memory and message passing, shared memory, and heterogeneous/hybrid models.
Select the appropriate parallel programming paradigm for a given problem.
Evaluate the gain of a parallel solution compared to its single-processor equivalent.
Develop a parallel solution that meets a given specification.
Understand the concept of execution thread and know its programming models.
Select the appropriate thread programming model for a given problem specification.
Know the synchronization mechanisms between threads. Understand and prevent their problems. Apply appropriate synchronization mechanisms to a given problem.
Develop an efficient and effective multi-threaded solution for a given problem specification.
Evaluate the gain of a multi-threaded solution compared to its single-threaded equivalent.

syllabus_topics: Presentation and State of the Art.
Performance Models and Analysis of Parallel Algorithms
Execution time, efficiency, speed-up, cost, scalability, etc.
Decomposition, assignment, balancing, overlapping, partitioning, etc. Relaxed algorithms, pipeline, master-slave, process farm and replicated, etc.
Concurrency: basic concepts, models and synchronization mechanisms. Parallelism: programming models. Accelerators and hybrid-heterogeneous solutions.

assessment_methods.method: Partial Exam (P1) on Performance and Design topics
Partial Exam (P2) on Concurrent and Parallel Environments topics
Work sessions (individual or group assignments, with evaluation phase involving submission or defense)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.5 * Theory + 0.5 * Practices. A minimum grade of 5 (out of 10) is required to pass. Evaluated activities not completed will receive a zero. If the total weight of uncompleted activities exceeds 50% of the total grade, the final grade will be "No presentado". For the extraordinary call, the evaluation consists of a theoretical exam (50%) and a practical exam (50%). A final grade of 5 or higher (out of 10) is required to pass.
